script.title: How Six Companies Built Hoover Dam Two Years Early
sentences: In 1931, workers started building a concrete dam 660 feet thick.
The Hoover Dam stood in Nevada's scorching Black Canyon, where summer heat reached 120 degrees.
No one had ever built a concrete structure this massive before.
Some of the engineering techniques they used were unproven.
A consortium called Six Companies hired over five thousand workers in extreme conditions.
Yet they handed the completed dam to the government in 1936, over two years ahead of schedule.
That is how Six Companies beat a seven-year deadline in 120-degree heat.

claims_en: In 1931 workers began constructing Hoover Dam, which is 660 feet thick at the bottom.
Hoover Dam is located in Black Canyon on the Nevada-Arizona border where summer high temperatures averaged 119.9 degrees Fahrenheit in 1931.
A concrete structure as large as Hoover Dam had never been built before.
Some techniques used to construct Hoover Dam were unproven at the time.
A consortium named Six Companies, Inc. managed the construction, with employment peaking at 5,251 workers in July 1934.
The dam was turned over to the federal government on March 1, 1936, over two years ahead of the seven-year schedule.
Six Companies completed the project ahead of their seven-year contract limit under extreme desert conditions.
